title: China's biggest apps are inviting the West closer into its insular internet economy
summary:
For decades, China's internet economy has been a gated-off party.
While China has long since invited foreign businesses to set up shop within its borders, its internet has been closed off.
Because China's digital payment ecosystem is integrated into these social media apps, payment in the country is a challenge for foreigners, too.
But recent developments have pointed to a trend of China finally opening its doors and letting foreigners take small steps into its internet economy.

title: Six months into Iran war, almost half of global oil flows from war zones
summary:
Six months ago, U.S. ‌and Israeli attacks on Iran triggered what has become the largest oil supply crisis on record, with no clear ​end in sight.
Not all of this year's supply disruptions happened at the same time.
With Saudi Arabia ​re-routing ​oil to the Red Sea and Gulf exporters ​sneaking oil secretly out of the ‌Strait of Hormuz, the current Gulf oil disruption stands at around 5 million to 7 million bpd, according to analysts' estimates.
The conflicts in the Gulf and Ukraine have also cut global refining capacity by about a tenth.

title: The UK and Ukraine have signed a declaration on AI-enabled military capabilities
summary:
Ukraine and the United Kingdom have signed a joint declaration on artificial intelligence partnership covering the development and deployment of AI-enabled military capabilities, according to the Ukrainian presidency’s account of talks in Kyiv between Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Andy Burnham.
“We will work together to build next-generation Armed Forces and accelerate development and deployment of AI-enabled military capabilities,” Zelenskyy said.
Neither side has published the text of the declaration or indicated what funding, if any, sits behind it.
What the AI declaration actually produces will depend on procurement rather than diplomacy.
Britain’s defence establishment has been slow to buy from startups even as capital has poured into European military technology, and a declaration signed in Kyiv does not by itself change a contracting process in Whitehall.

title: Vatican foreign minister, in Moscow, says Ukraine war must end
summary:
MOSCOW, Aug 25 (Reuters) - A senior Vatican official urged an end to the Ukraine war after ‌meeting in Moscow on Tuesday with Russian Foreign ‌Minister Sergey Lavrov in the first in-person talks between Vatican and ​Russian officials in five years.
Archbishop Paul Gallagher, the Vatican's foreign minister, said every day that the four-year Russia-Ukraine war continues, it "creates new victims ... and renders future reconciliation ever ‌more difficult."
"It is therefore ⁠urgent and necessary to end and to look beyond the conflict," he said, speaking ⁠next to Lavrov at a joint press conference following their meeting.
Gallagher, the Vatican's second-highest diplomatic official, had last visited Moscow for talks with Lavrov in 2021, before the start of the war.
Gallagher said on Tuesday ​the Vatican would "continue ​to provide strong spiritual, diplomatic, and humanitarian support by contributing to and offering a space for dialogue" ​to end ‌the war, which has raged for 4-1/2 years.

title: Bangladesh could consider joining Mecca pact, in test for foreign ties
summary:

It is being viewed positively," said junior foreign minister Humayun Kabir.
"They are inviting the leadership of Bangladesh, particularly Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, to come and participate," he told reporters on Monday.

title: US lawmakers urge Trump to ban Americans from aiding Chinese security agencies
summary:
By Alexandra AlperWASHINGTON, Aug 25 (Reuters) - Republican and Democratic lawmakers on Tuesday called on the Trump administration to bar American citizens and businesses ‌from supporting Chinese and Russian civilian intelligence and security agencies.
Congress approved a ‌law in 2018 banning Americans from providing support to foreign military intelligence agencies but leaving the door ​open to such aid for similar civilian-led organizations.
The Commerce Department and the Russian and Chinese embassies in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
